claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you have.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 8 years old, so yes, he's under 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful to know that you have an 8-year-old son named Alex.

Now, let me ask you:

**Do you live with Alex, or are you making financial contributions towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - you know, buying clothes, helping with things he needs, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you're making financial contributions towards his upkeep, I need to understand a bit more about the arrangement.

**Roughly how much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and how does that compare to the current Child Benefit payment rate?**

(For context, the current Child Benefit payment is £23.80 per week for the first child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's needs - so a bit more than the Child Benefit rate, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful to know. You're contributing £26 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £23.80 per week.

Now I have one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else made a claim for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final clarification question:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex is under 16** – he's 8 years old
- **You are responsible for him** – you're contributing £26 per week towards his upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit payment rate of £23.80 per week
- **You live in the UK**
- **No one else is claiming** – this is important, as only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child

Even though Alex doesn't live with you, your financial contributions are sufficient to establish that you're responsible for him under the Child Benefit rules. You can now go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
